name: l0_datamap_keyvalues
about: The map keyvalue pass (`walks/L0-r017.md`): CBaseEntity::ParseMapData 0x1009e280 dispatches one virtual slot-110 KeyValue per pair in authored order; CBaseEntity::KeyValue 0x1009e430 truncates the key at `#` (strchr 0x10431f30), runs its nine literal arms -- `rendercolor`/`rendercolor32` (FUN_101d0630 0x101d0630, three bytes of m_clrRender +0x1a0, alpha untouched) and `renderamt` (atoi, the alpha byte) only behind a CASE-SENSITIVE `key[0] == 'r'` guard (1009e4b6), `disableshadows` (atoi != 0 -> m_fEffects |= 0x20), `mins`/`maxs` (FUN_101d03e0 then FUN_100dc770 with the other side unchanged), `disablereceiveshadows` (|= 0x80), `angle` (atof; v < 0.0f -> __ftol(v) == -1 selects "-90 0 0" 0x10555578, any other negative "90 0 0" 0x10555570; else Q_snprintf "%f %f %f" of GetAngles()[0] (slot 221, the LOCAL +0x428 pitch), v, GetAngles()[2]; then the key becomes `angles`), `angles` (FUN_101d03e0 -> slot 218 SetAbsAngles 0x100b2510), `origin` (-> slot 216 SetAbsOrigin 0x100b2300) -- and then walks the datamap chain from slot 82 down baseMap with FUN_101a5a80 0x101a5a80: a row is a candidate only with FTYPEDESC_KEY 0x4 and a case-insensitive external-name match; the type switch parses per the ROW's fieldtype_t (INTEGER atoi: `3.9` is 3; COLOR32 FUN_101d0630 writes all FOUR bytes, a three-number colour leaving alpha 0; CUSTOM 10 is the output rows' CEventsSaveDataOps::vfunc4 0x100cdb20 -> FUN_100cd6d0 0x100cd6d0, which parses the six comma fields with FUN_100ccf90 and PREPENDS the action); an unknown key returns false and writes nothing. FUN_101d0310 0x101d0310 keeps parsed components and zero-fills the rest (`1 2` is (1, 2, 0)). CAISound::vfunc82 0x101bb4a0 answers datamap_CAISound (0x10599f48: `soundtype` INTEGER +0x450 SAVE|KEY, `InsertSound` INPUT, baseMap datamap_CBaseEntity). CBaseEntity::ReadKeyField 0x100acab0 (slot 121, `ent_dump`'s read) walks derived-to-base for a row with flags & 0x14 (KEY or OUTPUT), case-insensitive, never descending an embedded map, and FUN_100d0390 0x100d0390 keeps the row's type code: `rendercolor` reads COLOR32 (8), `angles` VECTOR (3), `targetname` STRING (2), `model` (MODELNAME 16) and `OnUseBegin` (CUSTOM 10) VOID 0 and true, `nosuch` / `Kill` (an INPUT row) / `solid` (embedded) false. `box`, `box2` (logic_relay rows on CBaseEntity's table) and `snd` (ai_sound) are created at run time with the keys below, so every site of the pass is traced. Reported as `fail`, an arm, a parse, a stored word or a read differs from retail's.

notes: Key order is the staged row's own `origin` / `angles` keys first (`ElysiumArena::AuthoredRow`: `angles` is `0 <-face> 0`, so `face: -20` authors `angles 0 20 0`; the reader refuses an `angles` key of its own), then the record's JSON order, so `angles` precedes `angle` (pitch and roll 0 are what the rewrite keeps around yaw 45), `effects` precedes `disableshadows`, `renderamt` precedes `rendercolor` (box) and `RenderColor` (box2). 37 = 0x25 = effects 5 | 0x20. 1293816842 = 0x4d1e140a = (10, 20, 30, 77): the lowercase arm wrote RGB and kept the earlier alpha 77 (0x4d). 1971210 = 0x001e140a = (10, 20, 30, 0): `RenderColor` skipped the case-sensitive `r` guard, reached row 19 through the walk, and the four-byte parse zero-filled the alpha over the earlier 44 (300 & 0xff). 12.7 cm = 5 Source inches: `origin#2` is `origin` after the `#` truncation and SetAbsOrigin took the parsed (0, 0, 5). The `m_OnUseEnd` row shows the six-field parser: an empty input is `Use`, `1.5s` reads 1.5, `times` 2 stays, field 5 is the Python text. A repeated key cannot be spelled in one JSON object, so the prepend order of two `OnUseBegin` keys and the `disableshadows 1` then `0` fold (retail keeps 0x20; the exporter's last-wins fold loses it, a named representation) are stated, not driven. Not driven: the `ent_debugkeys` print (a console diagnostic), the `Bad field in entity!!` arm (no CBaseEntity / CAISound KEY row has such a type; `never` asserts it stays silent), the dead KeyValue(float) 0x1009ebb0 / KeyValue(Vector) 0x1009eca0 overloads (no dispatch in vampire.dll), the `InsertSound` input (the input story).
